chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Benny Carter recordings for Bob Freedman; Flip Phillips's photograph gift
summary: Carter assembled top Los Angeles players to record songwriter Bob Freedman's tunes, and Flip Phillips gave Collins an old photo of himself with Lester Young.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Somewhere back, I think on our second tape, you mentioned a white singer who sang like Billy Eckstein, but you couldn't remember his last name.
Yeah, it was Bill Farrow. And he made this tune, it really made him famous. I mentioned it before, what was it -- well, okay.
I guess it's on tape number two. (Inaudible).

Yeah, but any way he later did quite a few things with Bob Hope. Bob Hope had this television show with Les Brown's band, and Bill Farrow was the featured vocalist on there. Very fine singer though, you know, But in thinking about Benny Carter, I don't know whether I mentioned before that I did quite a few recordings with Benny. This for Bob Freedman. This is a guy from Florida who was a song writer, and he wrote so many tunes, and he wanted to hear them all on records, so he wanted them all

recorded, and he wanted Benny to do them. And so Benny assembled the musicians and he had just about everybody that was anybody in Los Angeles on this day. And Bob Freedman brought Flip Phillips from Florida with him to do these recordings. And it was just nice seeing Flip after so many years and it was -- we were doing these tapes during the Christmas season, and on one -- tapes, this album, rather.

Yeah, but this particular date Flip brought me a Christmas present, and it was a picture, an old picture of Les Young, Prez and myself, playing, just the two of us. And it was just the greatest thing he could have done. He said, well John, I knew you were going to be on the date so I brought this from Florida just to give you because I knew you'd like to have it. And I have it. I had it framed, it's just a marvelous thing.
